trends.name: Cafe Imports Goes 100% Employee-Owned
trends.buzz: One of specialty coffee's biggest green-bean importers just became fully employee-owned. This is a huge win for the people who source, QC, and ship the beans you brew every morning.
trends.angle: Frame as a feel-good industry shift that connects home brewers to the supply chain. Celebrate worker ownership as good for coffee quality and ethics — no jargon, just 'the folks doing the work now own the company.'

trends.name: Cascara Fizz: The Coffee Cherry RTD Taking Off
trends.buzz: Cascara Cabinet is turning coffee cherry husks into a sparkling RTD drink. It's caffeinated, fruity, and a zero-waste win — plus it's just hitting shelves nationwide.
trends.angle: Position as a fun, approachable way to experience cascara without needing a brew recipe. Emphasize sustainability + flavor, not preciousness. 'If you love cold brew but want something lighter, this is your move.'

trends.name: Electrified Cold Brew Speeds Up Your Summer Sips
trends.buzz: Atomic Coffee and Overpotential teamed up to create cold brew that extracts in minutes using electrification tech. It's faster, cleaner-tasting, and opens up new brewing possibilities at home.
trends.angle: Make it exciting for gear nerds and beginners alike. Frame as 'cold brew without the 12-hour wait' — no pretense, just a practical innovation. Hint at future home brewers being sold if the tech scales.

trends.name: Solar-Powered Coffee Roasting Is Now a Real Thing
trends.buzz: A New Mexico experiment is using solar heat to roast coffee beans. It's early-stage but could change how roasters think about energy and sustainability — especially in sunny climates.
trends.angle: Frame as 'the future is weird and cool.' Celebrate the innovation without overpromising. Tie it to home brewing: 'The beans you buy tomorrow might be sun-roasted — and that's awesome.'

trends.name: New Study Links Coffee to Muscle, Fat & Testosterone
trends.buzz: Fresh research shows coffee consumption is associated with body composition and hormone levels. Whether you brew for gains or just love the ritual, coffee keeps surprising scientists.
trends.angle: Keep it light and inclusive — no bro-science. Frame as 'coffee does more than wake you up,' and invite curiosity. Avoid health claims; just celebrate the science as interesting, not prescriptive.

trends.name: MLB Pitcher's Espresso Machine Mystery Goes Viral
trends.buzz: Dodgers ace Tarik Skubal's espresso setup became a social media detective story. Fans are debating the machine, the grinder, and whether he pulls his own shots before games.
trends.angle: Lean into the fun. 'Same team' vibes — pros and beginners alike geek out over gear. Use it to normalize coffee obsession and show that even elite athletes care about their morning pour-over (or shot).

trends.name: SCA Invests $1M in UC Davis Coffee Research
trends.buzz: The Specialty Coffee Association just gave UC Davis a million dollars for a new research fellowship. Expect breakthroughs in agronomy, flavor science, and brewing tech in the next few years.
trends.angle: Frame as 'your coffee is about to get even better.' Celebrate investment in science as benefiting everyone — from farmers to home brewers. No gatekeeping: 'This research will level up the beans you buy.'

trends.name: Blends Build Loyalty, Micro Lots Get the Glory
trends.buzz: A new industry deep-dive argues that while single-origin micro lots dominate hype, it's blends that keep customers coming back. Consistency beats novelty for most home brewers.
trends.angle: Validate the everyday coffee drinker. Frame blends as smart, not boring. 'You don't need a $40 Gesha to make killer coffee — a great blend and good technique beat hype every time.'

trends.name: Should Coffee Invest More in Baristas as Automation Rises?
trends.buzz: As superautomatics and smart brewers flood the market, a new essay asks: are we investing enough in the humans who teach, inspire, and innovate? The debate is heating up.
trends.angle: Frame as relevant to home brewers: 'The people who taught you to brew deserve support, even as gear gets smarter.' Celebrate human expertise as irreplaceable, not threatened.

trends.name: World's Best Baristas Are Going on Tour
trends.buzz: Top competitive baristas are hitting the road with live demos, tastings, and Q&As. It's part masterclass, part coffee concert — and tickets are selling fast in major cities.
trends.angle: Make it accessible: 'You don't need to compete to learn from champions.' Frame as a fun, inclusive way to level up your brewing. Encourage people to grab tickets and geek out together.
